newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia urges NATO compromise on partnership deal.
newsitem.headline: Russia urges NATO compromise on partnership deal.

text.p: Russia urged NATO on Monday to show a greater willingness to compromise in negotiations on a partnership agreement between the two former Cold War foes.

On the eve of new talks in Moscow between Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov and NATO Secretary General Javier Solana, presidential press secretary Sergei Yastrzhembsky said Moscow needed to be sure the partnership would be on equal terms.
"Such an agreement must be reached on an equal basis, but not at all cost," Yastrzhembsky told Interfax news agency after Primakov had talks with President Boris Yeltsin in the Kremlin.
Some NATO members "are not showing enough desire to seek a compromise," said Yastrzhembsky, who this month was given additional responsibilities for coordinating foreign policy.

Moscow opposes NATO's plans to take in members from the former Soviet bloc but Primakov said last week that Yeltsin hoped to sign an agreement mapping out post-Cold War relations with the Western defence alliance on May 27.

Some Western diplomats say Moscow has toughened its negotiating stance even though Yeltsin seemed reconciled to the idea of NATO's expansion at last month's summit in Helsinki with U.S. President Bill Clinton.

Yastrzhembsky, echoing comments by NATO diplomats, said there had been progress in work on preparing documents for signing and reiterated Moscow's overall readiness to complete a substantial "binding" agreement.
Russia says NATO's plans to offer membership in July to some new members, expected to be Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic, endanger its security.
Moscow is seeking restrictions on the movement of NATO's military infrastructure into the new member states.
